chunks.arabic_text: وَسَأَلَ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Abu Basir asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: عَنْ قَوْمٍ مُحْرِمِينَ اشْتَرَوْا صَيْدًا فَاشْتَرَكُوا فِيهِ فَقَالَتِ امْرَأَةٌ رَفِيقَةٌ لَهُمُ اجْعَلُوا لِي مِنْهُ بِدِرْهَمٍ فَجَعَلُوا لَهَا

translations.en: About a group of people in ihram who purchased game and shared in it. A woman who was their companion said, "Give me a share of it for one dirham," and they gave her a share.
So he عليه السلام said: "Each person among them must offer a sheep."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning muhrims who collectively purchased hunted game while in the state of ihram. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام rules that each individual involved is liable for a sheep as expiation, indicating personal responsibility for participation in the prohibited act.
en.seo_question: What is the expiation for muhrims who jointly buy and share hunted game?

key_terms.مُحْرِمِينَ: people in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.اشْتَرَكُوا: they shared jointly or participated together
key_terms.بِدِرْهَمٍ: for one dirham, indicating a monetary share
key_terms.شَاةٌ: a sheep, specified here as the expiatory offering
